name: Affect-EEG Corpus Coding Scheme
description: A document-based coding scheme for released affect-EEG corpora. It separates what a corpus is released for from how that label was produced, so that two corpora with the same nominal task can be recognised as supporting different analyses.
principle: Code from documents only. Do not infer a value from general practice.
Absence of a statement is not a negative finding.
cannot judge is a valid value and is more informative than a guess.

fields.name: corpus
fields.label: Corpus identifier
fields.note: Short name used in the release or its descriptor.

fields.name: released_target
fields.label: Label the corpus is released for

definitions.assigned: One category per stimulus unit, identical for every participant, and this is the corpus's main task.
definitions.self-report: Each participant's own rating is the released target.
definitions.observer: Labels are scores that external raters gave to participants.
definitions.mixed: Labels for the same cell come from more than one source with no single main task.
definitions.cannot judge: The document does not state it.

fields.note: Ask what the distributed label file contains, not what was collected during the session.

fields.name: additional_stream
fields.label: Second annotation source released alongside the target

definitions.ratings: Participant ratings are released on top of an assigned target.
definitions.feedback: A participant-level score that is not an affect rating, for example an induction-success score.
definitions.observer: An observer annotation released alongside another target.
definitions.mixed: Streams of more than one kind appear together.
definitions.cannot judge: The document does not state it.

not_a_stream: an experimental condition fixed by design
stimulus metadata such as duration or language
fields.note: The test is whether a different role labels the same cell.

fields.name: ratings_per_stimulus
fields.label: How many ratings one participant gives per stimulus

definitions.one: A single rating per presented stimulus.
definitions.multiple: Several ratings per stimulus; record the number in notes.
definitions.time_resolved: An annotation at fixed intervals inside the exposure; record the interval in notes.
definitions.session_level: One annotation covering a whole session.
definitions.cannot judge: The document does not state it.

fields.note: A post-session summary score is session_level, not time_resolved. Only an in-exposure interval makes a label time resolved.

fields.name: stimulus_unit
fields.label: What one rating refers to

definitions.trial: One experimental trial, possibly containing several sub-events.
definitions.excerpt: One excerpt of a longer musical or audiovisual item.
definitions.game: One game session or game condition.
definitions.period: A defined time block, such as a pre- or post-task period.
definitions.exchange: One turn or exchange in an interaction.
definitions.other: None of the above; describe it in notes.
definitions.cannot judge: The document does not state it.

fields.note: When a release describes conditions rather than items, the unit is the condition, and the corpus cannot be pooled with clip-level corpora without a conversion rule.

fields.name: stimuli_shared
fields.label: Did all participants see the same stimuli?

definitions.yes: The same material was presented to every participant.
definitions.no: The document states that material differed between participants, for example own dialogues or participant-chosen media.

fields.note: Silence is cannot judge, never no.

fields.name: protocol_records_self_report
fields.label: Did the protocol collect a participant rating?

definitions.yes: The procedure includes a participant rating.
definitions.no: The document states that no participant rating was collected.
definitions.not established: The procedure is described but whether participants rated anything is not stated.
definitions.cannot judge: The document does not describe the procedure.

fields.note: not established requires a description of the procedure. If there is no procedure description at all, use cannot judge.

fields.name: release_description
fields.label: Does the release description mention participant-rating files?

definitions.explicitly describes: The release description names or lists participant-rating files.
definitions.does not mention: The description was read and contains no such mention.
definitions.not inspected: The description could not be reached.
definitions.cannot judge: The description was reached but is too vague to decide.

fields.note: does not mention never means the file does not exist. It records what the description says, not what the package holds.

fields.name: n_subjects
fields.label: Participant count
fields.note: Record the released or analysed count. If recruited, recorded and analysed counts differ, record the released count and put the others in notes.

fields.name: n_stimuli
fields.label: Stimulus count
fields.note: When the release describes conditions rather than items, record TBD and state the condition structure in notes.

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Evidence note
fields.note: Which document was read and which sentence decided the values. This is the only defence of the coding.

fields.name: cannot_judge_fields
fields.label: Fields answered with cannot judge
fields.note: Must list every field whose value is cannot judge, so that the share of undetermined fields can be counted.

checks.message: ratings is defined as participant ratings released on top of an assigned target, so released_target must be assigned or mixed.
time_resolved requires the interval to be recorded in notes, for example 'every 5 s'.
multiple requires the number of ratings per stimulus to be recorded in notes.
notes describes an in-exposure interval while the value is session_level. A post-session summary is not time resolved; check which one the release actually contains.
stimulus_unit other requires a description of the unit in notes.

then.value: (does not exist|no such file|no ratings? (were|was) released|withheld)

checks.message: does not mention records what the description says. It cannot support a statement that a file does not exist or was withheld.
TBD is reserved for counts. Use cannot judge for categorical fields.
no requires a statement in the document that no rating was collected. If the procedure is only described, use not established.
mixed needs a note naming the sources that coexist for the same cell.

reporting.count_of_undetermined: Report the number of fields answered cannot judge, per field and overall.
reporting.no_inference_rule: A TBD or cannot judge cell is reported as unreported, never filled by inference from other corpora.
reporting.unit_warning: Corpora whose stimulus_unit is a condition rather than an item cannot be pooled with item-level corpora without a stated conversion rule.
